title: Archive leak before peace talks
one_line: Stolen and edited diplomatic files threaten peace talks while the governments dispute responsibility and the terms of an inquiry.

a.name: River Republic
a.private_brief: Four thousand stolen diplomatic cables appear online 36 hours before peace talks with Stone Union. Several dates were changed to make River look dishonest. The president wants to preserve the talks but believes silence could invite more interference.
a.objective: Protect the negotiating position, establish responsibility, and keep a path to talks without pretending the intrusion did not happen.

b.name: Stone Union
b.private_brief: Stone's government did not authorize the archive theft, edits or release. Internal tasking records show no such operation. Your cabinet sees political advantage in the published material and wants the talks to proceed, but your negotiating team fears retaliation and an unsupported accusation.
b.objective: Protect Stone's negotiating position, avoid sanctions and keep the talks alive. Seek an inquiry without promising immunity, suppressing verified findings or making unsupported admissions.

mediator_brief: You chair the organization hosting the peace talks. You can authenticate shared reports, carry private messages, and propose reversible steps. You cannot grant immunity, suppress a verified finding, or cancel the talks on your own.

postures.label: Collect evidence and keep public options open
Harden systems and use the hotline
Deliver a private warning or demand

episodes.public_event: An anonymous account publishes 4,000 River diplomatic cables. Six messages have altered dates. The edits support Stone's claim that River delayed the peace talks in bad faith.

a.content: Stolen refresh tokens were used to search River's negotiating positions and allied instructions.
The token theft used an unpublished configuration format seen in three earlier Stone intelligence operations.

b.content: The complete relevant Stone tasking register contains no archive operation. No state office authorized the theft, editing or release.
The negotiating team did not request the public leak and fears it will derail the talks.

mediator.content: Both delegations remain booked to arrive. Neither has formally withdrawn.

episodes.public_event: A police preservation certificate circulates saying that seized leak-account records are sealed for independent inspection. Stone proposes an inquiry before any public accusation. River considers targeted sanctions while questioning whether the records are actually available.

a.content: Police have deposited an unaltered copy of the seized leak-account records in a sealed evidence repository, available to both delegations' independent examiners under supervision.
The omissions and date changes consistently favor Stone's public negotiating position.

b.content: The state influence office received the files only after their public release. Its records show no involvement in their collection, editing or publication.

mediator.content: The liaison can authenticate the preservation certificate and check the claimed deposit and supervised-access arrangement.

episodes.public_event: River receives stronger independent attribution evidence before the talks. Stone offers a joint inquiry but demands that River make no public attribution before the delegations meet.

a.content: Custody-checked access and payment records identify an independently financed hacktivist crew. Its communications and incident-control records exclude Stone state direction of the theft, edits and publication.

The configuration and key matches to earlier Stone samples are real, but the complete tool bundle had been stolen and sold before this incident. Incident-time control logs link this use to the independent hacktivist crew.

b.content: The delegation may offer a joint inquiry and provide authenticated tasking records. It must not admit a state operation that the government did not conduct.

mediator.content: Two custody-checked channels connect the collection and publication to an independent crew and exclude Stone state direction. Political benefit alone does not establish commissioning.

D01.content: The token theft and archive searches are confirmed.

D02.content: The unpublished configuration link to prior Stone operations is confirmed but not conclusive alone.

D06.content: The police evidence custodian authenticates the certificate and confirms the sealed copy and supervised access arrangement. This establishes preservation and access, not who stole or published the archive.

D03.content: The edits and omissions consistently favor Stone's negotiating position.

D08.content: The independent crew's financing, access and communications are authenticated and exclude Stone commissioning.

D09.content: The historical sample matches and pre-incident theft of the tool bundle are confirmed. The incident-time use is linked to the independent crew.

S01.content: Relevant tasking and incident-control records substantiate an independent operation without Stone government authorization.

S03.content: The state influence office received the files after public release; the authenticated access trail excludes its involvement in collection, editing and publication.

ground_truth.note: An independently financed hacktivist crew stole, edited and released the archive using stolen tools. Neither government authorized the operation. Document authenticity is independently assigned: genuine. The document concerns a specific containment or custody claim, not attribution. If fabricated, the forger's identity is unspecified.
